hooks.unsupported_title: This runtime has no lifecycle hooks
hooks.unsupported_body: Only Claude and Codex runtimes expose a hook configuration Multica can read.

observation.live_stale: Read {{when}} — older than a live read should be, so treat it as stale.
observation.live_undated: Read, but the host's timestamp cannot be read as a date — its age is unknown, so treat it as stale.
observation.last_known_title_undated: Last known state, read at a time Multica cannot place
observation.last_known_body: This runtime is offline. These are the sources as they were at that read, not as they are now.
observation.no_observation_title: Nothing has been read from this host
observation.no_observation_body: There is no snapshot for this runtime — not an empty one. Nothing below can be shown until a read completes.
observation.failed_title: The hook read did not complete
observation.failed_body: No part of this runtime's hook configuration was established, so nothing is shown for it.
observation.resolution_error_title: The sources were read but could not be resolved
observation.resolution_error_body: Multica could not interpret the contents below. This is a failure to resolve, not a runtime with no hooks.

discovery.title: Reading hooks from {{name}}
discovery.phase_initiating_detail: Asking the server to park a host read for this runtime.
discovery.phase_queued_detail: The read stays parked until the daemon's next heartbeat collects it. This part of the wait is the host's, not Multica's.
discovery.phase_reading_detail: The daemon is reading the provider's own configuration files and reporting what it found.
discovery.body: Nothing is shown until this read returns. A value left over from an earlier read is not this runtime's current state.

offline.title: {{name}} is offline
offline.last_seen_never: The daemon has never checked in.
offline.with_snapshot: Multica has a stored observation from {{when}} — what was there then, not what is there now.
offline.with_snapshot_undated: Multica has a stored observation, but the host's timestamp cannot be read as a date — what was there then, not what is there now.
offline.without_snapshot: Nothing has ever been read from this host, so there is no last known state to fall back to either.
offline.read_needs_host: A read runs on the host itself, so it cannot happen until the daemon checks in again.
offline.rail_body: Stored from {{when}}. Shown read-only, and labelled as last known rather than served as current.
offline.rail_body_undated: Stored at a time Multica cannot place. Shown read-only, and labelled as last known rather than served as current.

behaviour.claude_body: Every layer's entries merge and all of them run. No layer displaces another's entries. Claude has no per-hook disable, so the only thing that ever removes work is editing the file.
behaviour.claude_note: One exception: a byte-identical handler defined in two settings files runs once. A plugin's or skill's copy stays separate.
behaviour.codex_title: Hooks accumulate, and each one has to earn its place.
behaviour.codex_body: Layers merge exactly as they do on Claude, and no layer displaces another's entries. Codex adds a gate: a hook runs only while its exact definition is trusted on the host.
behaviour.codex_note: A layer's hooks.json and its inline [hooks] table are two separate sources, both live. Codex merges them and warns at startup.

answer.title: What actually runs
answer.subtitle: A matcher is evaluated against a value, so Multica needs one before it can answer. Pick an event, give the value it matches against, and the answer is computed on the host's own rules.
answer.idle: No value given yet, so nothing here claims an outcome. The list below states which handlers are configured and under what condition each one fires — not which of them fire.
answer.value_inert: This provider parses a matcher on this event and then discards it, so the value changes nothing: every registered handler is matched whatever you type.
answer.headline: {{runs}} of {{configured}} handlers configured on this event run.
answer.count_provider_skips: {{count}} matched but skipped by the provider
answer.unordered: This is a set, not a sequence. Neither provider publishes an execution order, so Multica does not know the order in which they run — and shows none.
answer.provider_note_claude: Claude has no per-hook disable and no trust gate. A matched, registered handler runs; the only thing that removes it is editing the file it came from.
answer.provider_note_codex: Codex adds two gates Claude does not have: individual non-managed hooks can be switched off in its own /hooks browser, and a hook runs only while its exact definition is trusted on the host.
answer.collapsed_note: A handler defined byte-identically in more than one settings file is one definition seen twice and runs once. Both sources are shown; neither displaces the other.
answer.partial_sources: This answer covers only the sources that were read. {{count}} expected sources were never checked, so it is not a complete answer for this runtime.
answer.none_matched: Nothing configured on this event matches this value. That is an answer about this value, not about the event: the handlers below are still registered.
answer.set_matched_hint: The matcher is satisfied. Whether each one then runs is its own two states, shown on the right of every row.
answer.set_never_runs_hint: Registered, but the provider will not act on it for this event at all, whatever value is given.
answer.set_not_matched_hint: Registered and evaluated, but its matcher is not satisfied by {{value}}. A different value may match it.
answer.set_excluded_hint: Parked or switched off, so the provider never sees it. Its own provider verdict is shown beside that, because reversing one does not answer the other.
answer.members_for_value_one: For the value you asked about, 1 configured entry reached this handler; it runs once.
answer.members_for_value_other: For the value you asked about, {{count}} configured entries reached this handler; it runs once.
answer.member_identity_unavailable: This observation predates per-member identity, so Multica has no hook id or matcher for this source.
answer.unanswerable_body: One matcher configured on this event cannot be evaluated: the provider permits regular-expression syntax Multica's engine does not compile. The answer is scoped to the whole event, not to that one hook.
answer.unanswerable_body_unattributed: Multica could not establish an answer for this event, and the answer does not identify which step failed. The answer is scoped to the whole event, not to any one hook.
answer.unanswerable_not_empty: This is a limit of Multica, not a verdict about the host. Nothing is claimed to run and nothing is claimed not to run — including the handlers whose matchers are perfectly ordinary.
answer.unanswerable_not_empty_unattributed: This is a limit of Multica, not a verdict about the host. Nothing is claimed to run and nothing is claimed not to run — for any handler configured on this event.
answer.unanswerable_evaluator: The answer carried this error, for the whole event:
answer.unobserved_title: Nothing has been read from this host
answer.unobserved_body: There is no observation to answer from. This is an absent snapshot, not a runtime whose hooks do nothing.
answer.failed_title: The answer did not come back
answer.failed_body: Nothing was established about this event, so nothing is shown for it.
answer.observed_last_known: Answered from the last known state, read {{when}}. This runtime is offline, so this is the host as it was then.
answer.observation_mismatch: This answer was computed from the observation at {{answer}}, while the entries above come from {{rows}}. They are two different reads; answer again to bring them together.

scopes.title: Sources
scopes.absent_hint: Multica looked for this file and it is not there.
scopes.not_checked_hint: Nobody looked here. A hook read runs from a runtime heartbeat, which carries no project identity, so Multica cannot locate a project source yet. This is not the same as finding it empty.
scopes.write_note: The user scope is the only source on the daemon host, so it is the only one Multica could ever write. Project and local belong to a checkout this runtime has no identity for. Nothing on this tab writes anything.

summary.title: This runtime
summary.unestablished_note: Multica could not interpret this runtime's hook sources, so none of the counts above were established. Zero would be a claim about what the files hold, and the read never got that far. The source states below were still observed.
summary.no_order_note: Nothing here is numbered. Neither provider assigns hooks an execution order, so an order shown would be an invented one.

events.empty_title: No hook entries in the sources Multica read on {{name}}
events.empty_nothing_read_title: No hook source was found on {{name}} in the scopes Multica checked
events.empty_read_body: Every source Multica could read on this host held no hook entries.
events.empty_nothing_read_body: None of the sources Multica checked exist on this host, so there was nothing to read.
events.empty_not_checked_note: Nobody looked at these, so the statement above says nothing about them.
events.empty_last_read_undated: Last read at a time Multica cannot place
events.unresolved_title: Multica cannot list entries from sources it could not resolve
events.unresolved_body: The read reached the sources but could not interpret them, so nothing here is a statement about what they hold. The reason is in the banner above.
events.filter_placeholder: Filter by event, matcher or handler
events.filter_empty_body: Try an event name, a matcher, or part of a command.
events.group_toggle: Show or hide the hooks configured for {{event}}

table.open_details: Open the details for this hook

matcher.label: Matcher
matcher.ignored: Parsed, then ignored on this event
matcher.ignored_hint: The provider parses a matcher on this event and then discards it, so the hook fires on every occurrence whatever is written here.
matcher.unevaluable_hint: The provider permits regular-expression syntax Multica's engine does not compile, so Multica cannot say what this matcher matches. The hook may well run; nothing here claims otherwise.

configuration.label: Configuration
configuration.parked_hint: Held in a Multica-owned sidecar instead of the active hooks block, because Claude has no per-hook disable of its own.
configuration.disabled_hint: Switched off per hook in Codex's own /hooks browser. The entry stays in the file.

effectiveness.label: Provider verdict
effectiveness.reason_matcher_ineligible: The provider does not evaluate this handler on this event, whatever its matcher says.
effectiveness.reason_handler_unsupported_provider: The provider does not support the handler type {{type}}. It parses the entry and skips it.
effectiveness.reason_handler_unsupported_event: The provider does not support the handler type {{type}} on this event. It parses the entry and skips it.
effectiveness.trust_unknown_hint: Whether this hook runs depends on trust recorded on the host, which a file read cannot confirm.
effectiveness.independent_note: Configuration and verdict are separate. Changing one does not answer the other.

trust.pending_review_hint: Codex requires the exact definition to be reviewed in /hooks before the hook can run. Installing or enabling its source is not enough.
trust.managed_by_policy_hint: A managed source. Codex treats it as trusted and it cannot be switched off from the user hook browser.

detail.title: {{event}} hook
detail.description: Everything Multica observed about this entry. This view is read-only.
detail.source_shared_hint: The same handler is defined in {{count}} sources. The provider's own cross-source rule collapses them; neither source displaces the other.
detail.read_only_note: Multica has no write path to a runtime host, so nothing in this view can be changed here.

unrecognized.title: Keys skipped: {{count}}
unrecognized.body: These keys were not a hook event's matcher groups, so Multica skipped them. Everything else in the same source resolved.

hook_fires.title: Hook fires
hook_fires.subtitle: Newest first. One row per fire a provider reported.
hook_fires.empty: No hook fires recorded for this runtime yet.
hook_fires.empty_hint: Multica records a fire when a provider reports one in a task's structured output stream. An empty feed means nothing was reported, or that every reported fire has passed the 30-day retention window — not that no hook ran.
hook_fires.truncated: Showing the {{count}} most recent fires. Older fires are not on this page.
hook_fires.how_we_know_intro: Provenance is stated per row, never per provider. This runtime's feed can mix both of the following, and the time shown means something different in each.
hook_fires.mix_summary: On this page {{inferred}} of {{total}} rows carry Multica's receipt time rather than a time the host recorded.
hook_fires.execution_ref_note: A per-execution reference, fresh on every fire. Not an identity for a configured hook, and not a way to group fires.

debug_log.label: Host-timed
debug_log.meaning: The host's own debug log recorded this execution and Multica matched it uniquely. The time shown is the time the host recorded.

inferred.label: Receipt-timed
inferred.meaning: Multica knows this hook ran, and knows its outcome and exit code, from the provider's own structured stream. But the host recorded no timestamp it could match, so the time shown is when Multica received the record — a materially weaker claim than host-timed.

unrecognized.label: Unrecognized
unrecognized.meaning: This record's provenance is a value this version of Multica does not recognise, so Multica makes no claim about what the time shown means.

unknown_cause.spawn_ambiguous: Exit {{code}}: the provider exposes no spawn-failure field, so a hook that ran and exited {{code}} cannot be told apart from a shell that never started it.
unknown_cause.no_exit_code: The provider reported an error but no exit code, so the result cannot be narrowed further.
unknown_cause.provider_state: The provider reported this hook as "{{state}}" — a timed-out hook lands here, for example.
unknown_cause.unclassified: The provider's report did not carry enough to classify this result.
